parsing_res_list.block_content: 2.Determine the values of the parameters indicated for the selected surface of the structure in ltem 1 above and calculate the following quantities:h/H,$I/L,L/H,L/R_{A}$ and $Z_{A}=R_{A}/W^{1/3}$

3.Refer to Table 2-3 (+) for the proper peak reflected pressure and impulse charts conforming to the number of adjacent reflected surfaces N and the values of $I/L$ .and $h/H$ of Item 2 above, and enter the charts to determine the values of $p_{r}$ and.$j_{d}/W^{1/3}$

In most cases, the above procedure will require interpolation for one or more of the parameters which define a given situation, in order to obtain the correct average reflected pressure and average reflected impulse. Examples of this interpolation procedure are given in Appendix 2A.

Because of the limitations in the range of the test data and the limited number of values of the parameters given in the above shock load charts, extrapolation of the data given in Figure 2-52 through Figure 2-149 may be required for some of the parameters involved. However, the limiting values as given in the charts for other parameters will not require extrapolation. The values of the average shock loads corresponding to the values of the parameters, which exceed their limiting values (as defined by the charts),will be approximately equal to those corresponding to the limiting values. The following are recommended procedures which will be applicable in most cases for either extrapolation or establishing the limits of impulse loads corresponding to values of the various parameters which exceed the limits of the charts:

1.To extrapolate beyond the limiting values of $Z_{A}$ , plot a curve of values of $p_{r}$ versus $Z_{A}$ for constant values of $L/R_{A},L/H,$ h/H and $1/L$ Extrapolate curve to include the value of $\mathsf{p}_{1}$ -corresponding to the value of $Z_{A}$ required. Repeat similarly for value of.$\overleftrightarrow{i_{r}}/W^{1/3}$

2.To extrapolate beyond the limiting values of $L/R_{A}$ extrapolate the given curve of $p_{r}$ versus $L/R_{A}$ for constant values of $Z_{A}$ $L/H$ , h/H and $1/L$ to include the value of $p_{r}$ corresponding to the value of $L/R_{A}$ .required. Repeat this extrapolation for value of.$j_{r}/W^{1/3}$

3.Values of $p_{r}$ and $i_{r}/W^{1/3}$ corresponding to values of L/H greater than 5 shall be taken as equal to those corresponding to $L/H=6$ for actual values of $Z_{A},h/H,$ and l/L but with a fictitious value of $L/R_{A}$ in which $R_{A}$ is the actual value and L is a fictitious value equal to 5H.
4.Values of $p_{r}$ and $i_{r}/W^{1/3}$ corresponding to values of l/L less than 0.10 and greater than 0.75 shall be taken as equal to those corresponding to $I/L=0.10$ and 0.75, respectively.
5.Values of $p_{r}$ and $i_{r}/W^{1/3}$ corresponding to values of h/H less than 0.10 and greater than 0.75 shall be taken as equal to those corresponding to $h/H=$ 0.10 and 0.75, respectively.
